title: External Dataset Evaluation and Generalization Audit

dataset_metadata.institution: Canadian Institute for Cybersecurity (CIC), University of New Brunswick (UNB)
dataset_metadata.citation: Sharafaldin, I., Habibi Lashkari, A., Ghorbani, A. (2018). 'Toward Generating a New Intrusion Detection Dataset and Intrusion Traffic Characterization.' Proceedings of the 4th International Conference on Information Systems Security and Privacy (ICISSP).
dataset_metadata.licensing_and_distribution: UNB requires interactive registration form with name, institutional affiliation, and email confirmation. Non-interactive scraping and redistributing raw CSVs via Git is restricted.
dataset_metadata.telemetry_modality: Network flow records generated via CICFlowMeter (birectional flow statistics).
known_limitations: Pure network flow telemetry: Zero host process, socket binding, or auth log context.
CICFlowMeter overflow bugs: produces Infinity and NaN in flow rate features, and negative duration values.
Duplicate records: Contains ~1% exact 5-tuple duplicates across capture windows.
Label casing and whitespace inconsistencies in raw CSVs.
High class imbalance: Benign traffic represents >80% of flows in most daily captures.
Targeted DoS/DDoS attacks dominate the attack volume, which are volumetric flooding rather than stealthy intrusions.

storage_requirements.MachineLearningCVE_csv_archive: ~500 MB compressed, ~2.5 GB uncompressed (8 daily CSV files)

schema_compatibility_audit.audit_name: AEGIS-ML 48-Feature Schema Compatibility Audit on CIC-IDS2017

sample_mappings.semantic_assumptions: Destination port accurately reflects target service type

schema_compatibility_audit.audit_verdict: 17 of 48 features (35.4%) are structurally unavailable in pure network flow datasets. Zero-filling or imputing unobserved endpoint features introduces severe distributional shift and invalidates the Phase 23 calibrated decision boundaries.

blocking_reasons: AEGIS-ML's calibrated model strictly requires 48 input features; CIC-IDS2017 provides only network flow telemetry.
17 features (35.4% of schema) represent endpoint processes, parent-child process ancestry, PAM/auth failures, and cross-layer socket bindings.

Silently imputing 0.0 for absent endpoint features corrupts calibrated probabilities: the model was calibrated on dual-telemetry synthetic data where endpoint indicators actively discriminate attacks.
Truncating the feature vector to 15 features is prohibited by model validation (ThreatClassifier enforces exact feature dimensionality).
Retraining or fine-tuning the production model simply to score higher on external benchmark data violates project integrity rules.
existing_model_transfer_evaluation.conclusion: Direct evaluation of calibrated_threat_classifier.pkl on CIC-IDS2017 is mathematically and scientifically INVALID. The model was trained on dual-telemetry events and cannot be transferred to single-modality network-only flow datasets without severe telemetry truncation.

reason: No CIC-IDS2017 CSV files found in datasets/cicids2017/. Official UNB download requires an interactive registration form at https://www.unb.ca/cic/datasets/ids-2017.html. Automated scraping without registration is prohibited by UNB. Evaluation infrastructure and schema audit are fully operational.
